gaps: The rollout prerequisite is missing. This checkout still runs the old `./forge` and has no `forge.toml`; `FORGE-WARM-1` has no roadmap dependency on the v1 switch, although the accepted rebuild decision says nothing else starts until that switch. The plan must name the switch as a prerequisite before USE-CODEX can run (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:104; plans/roadmap.json:1043; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:80-85; src/forge/repo.py:112-116).

The approval contract does not say how an unknown request is declined safely. The SDK forwards every server request to one handler, while the proposed stub sends only one approval request. Specify and test the response or fail-closed behavior for unknown methods before claiming every request is declined and never executes (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:45-47; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:234-238).

The turn log has no defined status when a process dies before Codex emits `turn/completed`. The draft requires one line for every turn, including errors and Ctrl-C, but permits status only from that event. Define the incomplete-turn record and recovery behavior without inventing a completed status (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:51-60).

A PID plus a check that the process is a Codex app-server does not identify this item's child: an unrelated Codex app-server can reuse the PID. The same PID-only stale-lock rule can mistake a reused PID for a live owner. The record and recovery tests need an identity that survives PID reuse (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:100; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:117-119; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:215-220).

Crash cleanup has an unrecorded interval. The SDK starts its app-server when the client is constructed, but RECORD writes the PID only after the thread starts. A crash between those steps leaves a child that neither the next `forge work` nor doctor can identify from the proposed record (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:58-60; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:100; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:215-218).

Approval refusal must precede the existing worker's status commit. `worker.work` currently commits `working` or `fixing` before entering its runner; placing RESUME's approval check only in that runner would change committed state while reporting that work was refused. The plan does not assign this preflight ordering (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:66-67; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:101; src/forge/worker.py:39-44).

Recovery of a turn left active in another app-server is assumed rather than specified. The plan needs an executable way for a new SDK client to identify, interrupt, and observe the terminal state of that prior turn, plus a test using two processes. Otherwise the promised `Next: forge work <item>` can repeatedly refuse without a recovery path (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:68-69; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:101; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:119-122).

The real-SDK acceptance check can be skipped everywhere that counts: the test skips without the SDK and its CI job is optional. Required checks can therefore pass without proving Done-when item 12 or the roadmap's requirement that the real smoke test passes. Name a required proof point or an explicit prerequisite that records a passing run (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:78-80; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:103; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:239; plans/roadmap.json:1034).

USE-CODEX has no test or other falsifiable proof for Done-when item 14. Its row changes the repository's worker selection and model routing but leaves Tests empty; the earlier throwaway settings probe does not verify the final committed settings in this repository (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:86-87; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:104; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:178-197).

The safety-hook demonstration lacks a reachable setup contract. Trusting a throwaway repository and running the hook health check do not establish that Codex approved and invoked that project's hook; the confirmed spec says Forge cannot observe hook approval. State how the UNPLUG check establishes hook activation before treating a blocked `gh pr merge` as proof (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:111-115; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:243-245; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:59-63).
contradictions: UNPLUG cannot meet 'nothing outside history uses or mentions the plugin' within its scope. Live `AGENTS.md`, `WORKFLOW.md`, `docs/FACTORY.md`, the confirmed delegation and coordinator specs, and the old `factory/` implementation still name or use it; the accepted switch preserves `docs/specs/` and `docs/decisions/`. UNPLUG scopes only three documentation files and a test, so the plan must identify which switch removes the other live references and which accepted documents remain authoritative (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:81-85; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:105; AGENTS.md:25; docs/specs/dual-coordinator-parity.md:76; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:80-85).

The plan needs to specify that both notes and story state remain untouched on every discard and failed read, and test those outcomes (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:70-74; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:102; src/forge/story.py:133-150).

The plan must name the switch as a prerequisite before USE-CODEX can run (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:104; plans/roadmap.json:1043; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:80-85; src/forge/repo.py:112-116).

The approval contract does not say how an unknown request is declined safely. The SDK forwards every server request to one handler, while the proposed stub sends only one approval request. Specify and test the response or fail-closed behavior for unknown methods before claiming every request is declined and never executes (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:45-47; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:234-238).

The turn log has no defined status when a process dies before Codex emits `turn/completed`. The draft requires one line for every turn, including errors and Ctrl-C, but permits status only from that event. Define the incomplete-turn record and recovery behavior without inventing a completed status (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:51-60).

A PID plus a check that the process is a Codex app-server does not identify this item's child: an unrelated Codex app-server can reuse the PID. The same PID-only stale-lock rule can mistake a reused PID for a live owner. The record and recovery tests need an identity that survives PID reuse (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:100; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:117-119; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:215-220).

Crash cleanup has an unrecorded interval. The SDK starts its app-server when the client is constructed, but RECORD writes the PID only after the thread starts. A crash between those steps leaves a child that neither the next `forge work` nor doctor can identify from the proposed record (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:58-60; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:100; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:215-218).

Approval refusal must precede the existing worker's status commit. `worker.work` currently commits `working` or `fixing` before entering its runner; placing RESUME's approval check only in that runner would change committed state while reporting that work was refused. The plan does not assign this preflight ordering (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:66-67; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:101; src/forge/worker.py:39-44).

Recovery of a turn left active in another app-server is assumed rather than specified. The plan needs an executable way for a new SDK client to identify, interrupt, and observe the terminal state of that prior turn, plus a test using two processes. Otherwise the promised `Next: forge work <item>` can repeatedly refuse without a recovery path (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:68-69; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:101; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:119-122).

The real-SDK acceptance check can be skipped everywhere that counts: the test skips without the SDK and its CI job is optional. Required checks can therefore pass without proving Done-when item 12 or the roadmap's requirement that the real smoke test passes. Name a required proof point or an explicit prerequisite that records a passing run (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:78-80; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:103; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:239; plans/roadmap.json:1034).

USE-CODEX has no test or other falsifiable proof for Done-when item 14. Its row changes the repository's worker selection and model routing but leaves Tests empty; the earlier throwaway settings probe does not verify the final committed settings in this repository (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:86-87; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:104; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:178-197).

The safety-hook demonstration lacks a reachable setup contract. Trusting a throwaway repository and running the hook health check do not establish that Codex approved and invoked that project's hook; the confirmed spec says Forge cannot observe hook approval. State how the UNPLUG check establishes hook activation before treating a blocked `gh pr merge` as proof (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:111-115; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:243-245; docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:59-63).

UNPLUG cannot meet 'nothing outside history uses or mentions the plugin' within its scope. Live `AGENTS.md`, `WORKFLOW.md`, `docs/FACTORY.md`, the confirmed delegation and coordinator specs, and the old `factory/` implementation still name or use it; the accepted switch preserves `docs/specs/` and `docs/decisions/`. UNPLUG scopes only three documentation files and a test, so the plan must identify which switch removes the other live references and which accepted documents remain authoritative (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:81-85; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:105; AGENTS.md:25; docs/specs/dual-coordinator-parity.md:76; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:80-85).

The draft says a failed or interrupted cold read writes no notes, but its READER task also says the existing discard rule stays without assigning any change to the `forge read` path's current state write after a successful model response. The plan needs to specify that both notes and story state remain untouched on every discard and failed read, and test those outcomes (plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:70-74; plans/FORGE-WARM-1-draft.md:102; src/forge/story.py:133-150).
